Subject: Pen test acceptance window and methodology details

Hi Naomi,

Hope you9re well. We're finalizing our vendor risk review for Acme Analytics and need to confirm a couple of items before we proceed: 

1) Acceptance window: We typically accept penetration test reports dated within the last 12 months. Can you confirm whether Redwood accepts tests up to 12 months old, or do you require a more recent test (e.g., within 6 months) for our procurement?

2) Methodology/coverage: Please confirm the methodology standards used (OWASP Top 10, NIST, CREST-equivalent), whether remote code execution/privilege escalation checks are included, and whether infrastructure and authentication services (SSO, token stores, KMS access) are in-scope.

3) Firm credentials: If you have a short vendor profile or SOC/attestation from the testing firm, please attach. Our security team will want the firm profile and a short statement on scope/assumptions.

If useful, you can attach a redacted executive summary of the last test. We do not need the full PII-bearing workpapers.

Would appreciate a response by EOD next Tuesday so we can keep our procurement timeline.

Best,
Lucas Green
Sr. Vendor Risk Manager
Acme Analytics

Hi Lucas,

Thanks for the clear list. Quick answers up front:
- Acceptance window: Redwood generally accepts a pen test executive summary up to 12 months old for standard procurement reviews. For higher-risk integrations (broad network connectivity or privileged data access) we ask for a test within 6 months or evidence of mitigation verification.
- Methodology: Our most recent engagement followed a hybrid approach (OWASP Top 10 + infrastructure checks aligned to NIST SP 800-115). The scope covered external and internal network tests, authenticated web app testing, SSO flow checks (SAML/OAuth), and privilege escalation scenarios.
- Firm credentials: I attached a redacted executive summary from our last test and the vendor9s firm profile. The vendor we used (CyberShield Assess) is CREST-aligned in practice; they provided CV excerpts for lead testers and proof of professional liability insurance.

I9m looping in Mina from Security to confirm there are no additional redline requirements for Acme's use case. Karthik, FYI on timeline.

Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Security & Compliance Manager, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood-pen-test-2025-summary.pdf, cybershield-firm-profile.pdf

Hi Lucas / Naomi,

Thanks for the context. A couple of clarifications from Security: 

- For Acme9s typical integration (data ingestion API + webhooks), 12 months is acceptable provided the executive summary shows no open criticals and the remediation timeline for any high findings was closed within 30 days of discovery.
- We require the test to include authenticated application tests and any credential/secret-management assessments; if the summary does not explicitly state those, please flag and we will request a short addendum.
- The pen test should document whether the assessment exercised service accounts and KMS access patterns. If not, we may ask for a focused retest of those controls prior to go-live.

If you can confirm there are no open criticals and share the lead tester9s CV (redacted), we can sign off.

Mina Haddad
Director, Security Compliance
Redwood Inference
